profile_headline: Data Analytics and Machine Learning Instructor at Google
post_content:
Slow down not to work less. But slow down to have time to think if you are
working on right things and to think if you are working right. I too was
addicted to working and I was closeminded to not realize that it was
ineffective. But luckily last week I tried experimenting to slow down and
actually focus on a select few things instead of working on many things and it
worked great. Before I got amount of work work done on multiple things, now I
got more impactful work done because of focusing on fewer but important
things. My last week's experiment is as follows: I decided to focus on just 3
things for the entire week. And using Pomodoro, I tracked the work. I faced
two major problems. 1\. First Problem - I found it very difficult to focus on
one thing, my mind was rebelling and getting distracted. 2\. Second Problem -
I got exhausted just by focusing for 1 hour. I realized 1 hour of focused work
is more exhausting than 10 hours of unfocused work. So, I plan to train my
brain to focus longer by meditation and get used to working for longer
duration by simple repitition. From my research I have found out, 3 hours of
focused work per day is a great number. Quality definitely beats quantity. :)

post_content:
I love nature and quote examples from nature. Here is a graph showing life
expectancy of mammals versus their gestation period. Interesting find : If a
species has an life expectancy of 25 years, then it must have had an gestation
period of 200 days - approx 7 months. In simple words, if baby has to survive
for 25 years, mom has to nurture baby inside body for more than 7 months. You
might be thinking why biology now - but the same rules of nature apply for
startups. Taking time to build the product slowly with feedback from
customers/clients and constantly improvising it over the time and scaling
after a lot of small success is what nature is trying to teach us !! Scaling
cannot happen from Day 1 or 100. I follow this with heart. Our product
improvisation, customer feedback comes first before scaling !! Tagging my fav
Li guide Dr Aniruddha Malpani as he quotes the same many times. You points

There was a very brilliant boy, \- He always used to score 100% in most of the
subjects. \- Later on, he got admission in IIT \- Landed a high paying job \-
Married a Beautiful Tamilian Girl. \- Had a big house and a handful of luxury
cars He had everything that made him successful, but quite a few years ago he
ended up committing suicide after shooting his wife and children. So, WHAT
WENT WRONG? California Institute of Clinical Psychology Studied his case and
found exactly what was wrong with him. The researchers found that somehow he
lost his job and failed to get any further opportunities. Even after declining
his salary graph, he failed to land a job. His family managed to survive for a
few months, but considering the fact that they had no money left, both he and
his wife decided to commit suicide. He first shot his wife and children and
then shot himself. The case concluded that the man was programmed for
successes but he was not trained for handling failures. This is why failure is
a part of success. if you never fail in your life then that is also a failure.
